news.title: mimalloc: A new, high-performance, scalable memory allocator for the modern era
news.summary_raw:
mimalloc is an open-source, modern, scalable memory allocator that is a drop-in replacement for malloc and free. It is relatively small (~12K lines), with clear internal data structures, and is easy to build and integrate into other projects. It provides bounded worst-case allocation times (up to OS primitives), bounded space overhead, low internal fragmentation, and minimal contention by relying almost exclusively on atomic operations.
The post mimalloc: A new, high-performance, scalable memory
news.summary: Microsoft Research has released an open-source memory allocator called mimalloc, providing high-performance and scalability. This allocator is a drop-in replacement for malloc and free, offering bounded allocation times, minimal space overhead, and low fragmentation.
news.enterprise_use: While mimalloc is primarily a system-level allocation tool, IT engineers should not directly act on this. However, it showcases advancements in memory management that could lead to the development of more efficient tools for managing memory-intensive tasks in enterprise environments. Inaction would mean missing potential improvements in memory allocation that could positively impact large-scale computing infrastructures.
